acme_ops: Hey team — noticed weird behavior after yesterday's rollout. Same user session sometimes gets different intents back-to-back for the same prompt. Example: two near-identical requests returned different answers in one conversation.

acme_ops: This started ~18:20 UTC right after you pushed the q4 rollout. Not a huge volume but it's affecting our billing and UX.

sara_support: Sorry — that sounds bad. Can you paste a minimal repro (request payload + session id) and one example pair of responses?

acme_ops: sure. session id = sess_7f9c2; payload below:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"session_id":"sess_7f9c2","model":"redwood-7b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the policy in two bullets."}] }'
```

acme_ops: Response A (first call):
```json
{"reply":"Policy prohibits X and Y. Summary: 1) Do not share PII. 2) Escalate breaches.", "meta":{"x-model-variant":"redwood-7b-vanilla","request_id":"r_001"}}
```

acme_ops: Response B (second call, same payload a few seconds later):
```json
{"reply":"Policy allows limited sharing of data with consent. Summary: 1) Obtain consent. 2) Log disclosures.", "meta":{"x-model-variant":"redwood-7b-q4-fallback","request_id":"r_002"}}
```

acme_ops: So same session, same payload, but different model-variant header and contradictory outputs.

sara_support: Thanks — that looks like routing to a fallback variant mid-session. We recently enabled a capacity-sparing fallback policy for low-priority tenants in the rollout. We'll triage. @kyle_ml can you check model routing logs for sess_7f9c2 and timing around 18:20 UTC?

kyle_ml: on it. Quick note: fallbacks can be triggered by latency spikes or capacity reclaim; they shouldn't mix within a single session but I remember an edge-case where cache keys weren't strictly session-scoped.

jamie_sre: Deploy bot shows a canary patch rolled at 18:15 UTC:

deploy-bot: Deployed redwood-runtime v3.12.4 -> traffic-policy=v2-canary (deploy-id=dep_1128)

jamie_sre: I'm pulling routing traces now. If cache or routing policy used request-level keys instead of session-level, one request could be served by stable pool and next hit fallback pool.

anita_cs: Customer wants immediate mitigation. Can we force-session-pin for sess_7f9c2 or globally disable fallback for their org until we fix? Their org id: org_acme_22.

kyle_ml: We can set a temporary override: routing.override.org_acme_22 = prefer=stable, fallback=false — that'll be immediate. I'll apply and monitor.

sara_support: acme_ops, we'll apply the override and let you know. Can you confirm whether you observed any other session ids with the behavior? Even a couple helps scope.

acme_ops: Thanks. We have two more sessions: sess_81a5 and sess_b12f. Both showed variant header mix within same chat. Please patch asap.

kyle_ml: applied override at 18:34 UTC. I'll also add a guard to ensure the session cookie is included in cache key for routing decisions.

jamie_sre: Quick repro notes for the infra ticket: observed routing decision sequence for r_001 -> stable pool (model redwood-7b-vanilla); r_002 -> fallback pool (redwood-7b-q4-fallback). Trace shows fallback allocation triggered by a short-lived autoscaler reclaim on pool-3.

kyle_ml: Root cause hypothesis: rollout changed pool tagging for q4 quantized variants; autoscaler reclaimed capacity and fallback policy allowed cross-session mixing because session id was not in the routing key for some lanes. Fix: ensure session_id is in routing key and make fallbacks session-consistent.

sara_support: Plan: (1) temporary org override (done), (2) hotfix to include session_id in routing key and disallow cross-session fallback mixing, (3) revert canary traffic-policy if needed. ETA for hotfix?

kyle_ml: I'll push a hotfix branch now, aim for staging tests by 20:30 UTC, hotfix rollout 21:00 UTC if tests pass.

anita_cs: I'll update the customer with the mitigation and estimated ETA. acme_ops — sorry for the disruption. We'll follow up with a postmortem and the specific rollback timeline.

acme_ops: Appreciate it. Please keep us in the loop — our product team is on standby. :handshake:
